module_name: Meta Content Library and Research Environments: Gated Access and Cost Reality
module_description: Module 5 deals with the hardest access case: Meta. Students learn what Meta Content Library / Content Library API actually provides to academic institutions (near real-time public Facebook/Instagram content, gated to qualified institutions, no fee), how Meta Secure Research Environment and SOMAR-type enclaves work, and what changed when free research compute ended and per-team fees started in 2026. The module ends with cost-aware alternatives for labs.
core_concepts: Institutional gating and eligibility of Meta research access
Content Library API capabilities and limits
Secure research environments / virtual data enclaves
Budget reality for university labs in 2026
Fallbacks: open protocols, archives, third-party datasets
learning_outcomes: C3 Describe eligibility and process for Meta research access
C4 Evaluate cost and access options for a proposed study
C3 Explain enclave constraints (no raw data export) and workarounds
methods_models: Feasibility analysis of access route; budget/compute planning; metadata-first study design
Method emphasis: designing a study that is feasible without raw export
evaluation_metrics: Feasibility/design memo graded on completeness of access route and cost estimate
pitfalls_limitations: Assuming access is automatic; assuming raw export is possible from enclaves; ignoring that Meta's release is selective and can be revoked
tools_stack: Meta Content Library documentation, SOMAR/enclave tutorials, budget spreadsheet, request templates
commercial_platforms: Walkthrough of the application form and eligibility criteria; costing exercise
tools_access_cost: Meta Content Library is free for qualified academic institutions; free research compute in SOMAR's enclave ended 31 Dec 2025 with per-team monthly charges reported from Jan 2026 (about USD 371) - verify current terms before planning
lab_activities: Submit a practice access request draft (eligibility statement, data need, security plan)
datasets_apis: Meta-topic sample via a sponsored collaborator or a public export; otherwise substitute topic samples
assessment_methods: Written analysis/design document plus a short quiz; graded on correctness of concepts and quality of justification
data_collection_workflow: Define the question -> choose platform and access route -> collect via API or permitted scrape -> archive raw with checksums -> clean and document schema -> analyse -> preserve dataset and code
textbooks: Guides on text and data mining with social media data (UNC/JHU library guides)
key_papers: Meta Content Library as a Research Tool (ACM, 2024-2025 papers)
Bellingcat toolkit note on Meta Content Library enclave pricing
trends_2024_2026: 2024-2026: the field split into 'gatekeepers' (Meta, X commercial tiers) and 'open access' (Bluesky, archives); teaching feasibility is now a primary learning outcome
industry_relevance: Social media analyst, market-insights researcher, and data-journalist roles; this module is used for social listening, brand/issue monitoring, and audience research, and is referenced by industry certifications such as Meta Blueprint, Hootsuite Social Marketing, and Google Analytics.
localization_context: Taught with Indonesian-language material (IndoBERT/IndoRoBERTa/NusaBERT, InSet lexicon, Indonesian social datasets) so students can reproduce the analysis on local corpora; comparisons are made against Anglocentric benchmarks whose labels often transfer poorly.
ethics_regulation: Platform Terms of Service, UU PDP No. 27/2022 (Indonesian personal data protection), GDPR for EU-origin data, and IRB-style review for any data involving private individuals; public is not the same as consentable for social data.
case_study_scenarios: You need Facebook data for an election-disinformation study with a zero budget - what is your route?
